questions.question: A linear map $A\colon V\to W$ has $[A]_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B}}=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ for ordered bases $\mathcal{B}$ of $V$ and $\mathcal{C}$ of $W$. A vector $\boldsymbol{v}\in V$ has $[\boldsymbol{v}]_{\mathcal{B}}=(1,-1)^{\top}$. What is $[A\boldsymbol{v}]_{\mathcal{C}}$?

Let $P_2$ be the real polynomials of degree at most $2$, with ordered basis $\mathcal{B}$, and let $\mathcal{C}$ be an ordered basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$. For an arbitrary real $2\times3$ matrix $M$, how many linear maps $A\colon P_2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfy $[A]_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B}}=M$?
options: Exactly one, but only when $M$ has rank $2$
Infinitely many, since only basis images are fixed
Exactly one, but only when $\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C}$ are standard
Exactly one, for every such matrix $M$

questions.question: Let $R\colon\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$, $R(x,y)=(-y,x)$, the quarter turn. With $\mathcal{B}=(\boldsymbol{e}_1,\boldsymbol{e}_2)$ and $\mathcal{C}=(\boldsymbol{e}_2,-\boldsymbol{e}_1)$ one finds $[R]_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B}}=I_2$. What may be concluded about the eigenvalues of $R$?
options: $R$ has the eigenvalue $1$, because the diagonal entries of $I_2$ equal $1$.
Nothing from this matrix: eigenvalues are read from $[R]_{\mathcal{B}}$ with one basis.
$R$ is the identity map, because its representing matrix is $I_2$.
$\boldsymbol{e}_1,\boldsymbol{e}_2$ are eigenvectors, since each $R\boldsymbol{e}_j$ is a basis vector.

questions.question: Let $V$ be the space of real $2\times2$ matrices with ordered basis $(E_{11},E_{12},E_{21},E_{22})$, where $E_{ij}$ has a $1$ in position $(i,j)$ and zeros elsewhere. What is the matrix representation of the linear operator $T(X)=X^{\top}$ in this basis?
options: The $4\times4$ identity matrix, since $T$ maps each $E_{ij}$ to a basis matrix
The $2\times2$ matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, since $T$ swaps the off-diagonal entries
The $4\times4$ matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,1)$, since $T$ flips the off-diagonal part
The $4\times4$ matrix that swaps the second and third coordinates and fixes the others
